items.title: A sacred pipe returns to Whitecap Dakota First Nation after 135 years
items.description: More Indigenous communities across Canada are reuniting with items that were taken or given away generations ago. The Vatican and the Canadian Catholic Church are reportedly working on an agreement to return about 100,000 Indigenous items Catholic missions sent to Rome in the 1920s.

items.title: Pilot killed in Ontario mid-air collision was taking part in training flight: TSB
items.description: The Transportation Safety Board of Canada says the pilot killed in a mid-air collision on Saturday was taking part in a training exercise.

items.title: Federal government plans to invest up to $5.45M to help grow women's soccer in Canada
If cloned meat enters the food supply, will Canadians know?
items.description: Meat from the offspring of cloned animals is entering Canada's food supply without safety reviews or mandatory labelling.

items.title: Domestic abusers are weaponizing B.C.'s housing crisis, report reveals
Is Quebec serious about climate change? New government bill raises questions
items.description: A new government bill aimed at reducing bureaucracy and increasing state efficiency could take a bite out of Quebec's ability to fight climate change. Under the proposed legislation, the finance minister will be allowed to divert surpluses from the province's Green Fund to other unrelated government programs.

items.title: Edmonton doctor says inner-city TB outbreak low risk to general public
items.description: The head of Alberta's tuberculosis clinic says an outbreak in Edmonton's inner-city is is of little risk to Edmontonians at large.

items.title: Manitoba Government Receives Report on Future of Technology, Innovation and Productivity
Police seek suspects of Upper Canada Mall jewelry store robbery
items.description: Two security guards and an unknown number of police officers were pepper sprayed Saturday afternoon as they pursued suspects in a jewelry store robbery at a mall in Newmarket, Ont.

items.title: Carney says Louis Riel's legacy 'helps to unite' Canada at event marking Métis leader's execution
items.description: Prime Minister Mark Carney laid a wreath at the grave of Louis Riel to mark the 140th anniversary of the Red River Métis leader's execution at a ceremony in Winnipeg on Sunday morning.

items.title: U.S.-based liqueur brand Sour Puss moves some production to Canada amid ongoing trade war
items.description: Chief political correspondent Rosemary Barton speaks with Andy England, CEO of Phillips Distilling Company, about his company's decision to move production of Sour Puss liqueur to Montreal after being taken off the shelf over the trade war.

items.title: Banff’s infamous grizzly ‘The Boss’ continues to dominate Bow Valley — but he’s got competition
items.description: Bears No. 122 and 136, known as The Boss and Split Lip respectively, are arguably two of the most famous grizzlies in Canada. The Boss is currently considered Banff National Park's dominant grizzly bear, while the younger Split Lip has been challenging him for the top spot.

items.title: Police Presence at Health Sciences Centre 24-7 to Protect Health-Care Workers and Patients
Weekend transit shutdown cancelled in Montreal as union, STM reach tentative deal
items.description: The public transit strike which would have shut down bus and Metro service in Montreal for the weekend has been cancelled after a last-minute tentative deal was reached Friday night.

items.title: Photos: Electronic powerhouses Kaytranada and Justice co-headline Rogers Arena
items.description: The DJ and the French duo combined for a memorable show.

items.title: Liberals 'ready for an election' if budget vote fails, says government whip
First Nation in northern Alberta sheltered in place overnight as RCMP searched for 3 robbery suspects
items.description: A First Nation in northern Alberta had to shelter in place overnight, after RCMP spotted three people near the community Saturday evening who were believed to be armed, having allegedly robbed several guns and shot at someone earlier that day.

items.title: Joint Statement By Prime Minister Mark Carney And Premier Wab Kinew On Federal-Provincial Collaboration Regarding Port Of Churchill Plus
Saskatchewan Roughriders, Montreal Alouettes' fans ready for Grey Cup face-off
items.description: The Saskatchewan Roughriders are hoping to get their fifth title in franchise history, while the Montreal Alouettes are wanting their second Grey Cup championship in three years.

items.title: N.B. faces snowfall warnings as N.S., N.L. brace for high winds
items.description: Snowfall warnings are in place for New Brunswick, with wind warnings in place for parts of Nova Scotia and Newfoundland and Labrador.

items.title: Alouettes hoping Bomber fans ‘adopt’ them Sunday
items.description: Alexandre Gagne figures his Montreal Alouettes might gain new fans in Sunday's Grey Cup against the Saskatchewan Roughriders.

items.title: Burnaby apologizes for decades of discrimination against people of Chinese descent
items.description: Burnaby has formally apologized for decades of discrimination against people of Chinese descent, pledging long-term action to address historic harm.

items.title: Divers seeking lost shipwreck near Toronto find an even older mystery
items.description: An exploration dive team seeking the century-old wreck of the Rapid City has instead found a much rarer prize: a virtually undisturbed vessel, potentially dating back to the first half of the 19th century.

items.title: B.C. NDP backs Premier David Eby's leadership at convention with 82 per cent support
items.description: Premier David Eby has faced criticism within his party for his promise to fast-track resource projects and for the eight-week strike by the B.C. General Employees Union. Despite that, New Democrats backed his leadership with 82 per cent support at this weekend's NDP leadership convention.

items.title: Montreal Carabins thump Saint Mary's Huskies to advance to Vanier Cup game
items.description: Mathieu Barsalou ran in four touchdowns as the Montreal Carabins defeated the Saint Mary's Huskies 49-19 on Saturday in the Uteck Bowl.
